title.zh: 星星为什么会一闪一闪
title.en: Why Do Stars Twinkle?

content.zh: 星星的光要穿过地球的空气才能到我们眼睛里。空气一直在流动，忽冷忽热，光被推得歪来歪去，看起来就像在眨眼睛。
content.en: Starlight must pass through our air to reach us. The moving air bends the light this way and that, so the stars seem to twinkle.

title.zh: 太阳为什么总也烧不完
title.en: Why Does the Sun Never Burn Out?

content.zh: 太阳不是在"烧东西"，而是中心把氢变成氦，放出巨大的光和热。它还有够用几十亿年的氢，所以不会马上烧完。
content.en: The sun is not burning fuel like a fire. Deep inside it turns hydrogen into helium, releasing light and heat. It has hydrogen for billions of years yet.

title.en: What Is a Shooting Star?

content.zh: 太空里有许多小石块，飞进地球空气时和空气猛烈摩擦，变得又烫又亮，划出一道光。大多数还没落地就烧没了。
content.en: Small rocks in space rub hard against our air when they fall in. They get so hot that they glow and streak across the sky. Most burn up before landing.

title.en: What Is a Black Hole?

content.zh: 黑洞是引力特别特别大的地方，连跑得最快的光都逃不出来，所以它看起来黑黑的。它并不是一个真的洞。
content.en: A black hole is a place with gravity so strong that even light cannot escape, so it looks black. It is not a hole you could fall through.

title.zh: 地球为什么不会掉下去
title.en: Why Does Earth Not Fall Down?

content.zh: 太空中没有"上"和"下"，也没有地面可以掉下去。地球一直绕着太阳转，太阳的引力拉住它，它就稳稳地跑在轨道上。
content.en: In space there is no up or down, and no floor to fall to. Earth keeps moving around the sun, and the sun’s gravity holds it in its path.

title.zh: 我们为什么只看到月亮的一面
title.en: Why Do We Only See One Side of the Moon?

content.zh: 月亮自己转一圈的时间和绕地球转一圈的时间刚好一样长，所以它总是用同一面朝着我们，背面我们在地球上永远看不到。
content.en: The moon takes exactly as long to spin once as to circle the Earth. So it always keeps the same face towards us, and we never see the far side.

title.zh: 土星为什么有一圈光环
title.en: Why Does Saturn Have Rings?

content.zh: 土星周围围着无数冰块和石头，大的像房子，小的像沙粒。它们绕着土星转，从远处看连成一圈亮亮的光环。
content.en: Countless chunks of ice and rock orbit Saturn, some house-sized and some like grains of sand. From far away they look like one bright ring.

title.zh: 彗星为什么拖着长尾巴
title.en: Why Do Comets Have Long Tails?

content.zh: 彗星是个"脏雪球"，飞近太阳时受热，里面的冰变成气体往外喷，被太阳风吹向后方，就拖出一条长长的尾巴。
content.en: A comet is a dirty snowball. Near the sun it warms up and its ice turns to gas, which the solar wind blows backwards into a long tail.

title.en: Why Is Mars Red?

content.zh: 火星的地面上全是含铁的尘土，铁生锈以后是红褐色的，整颗星球看上去就是红色的，像一颗生锈的大石头。
content.en: Mars is covered in dust containing iron. When iron rusts it turns reddish-brown, so the whole planet looks red, like a rusty rock.

title.en: Is the Milky Way a River?

content.zh: 银河不是河，而是无数颗星星挤在一起，密得连成一条亮带。我们住在银河系里面，所以它看上去像横过天空的一条河。
content.en: The Milky Way is not a river. It is countless stars packed so tightly that they form a bright band. We live inside it, so it looks like a river across the sky.

title.en: Where Do Stars Go in the Daytime?

content.zh: 星星一直挂在天上，白天也没走开。只是太阳把空气照得太亮，星星那点光比不过太阳光，我们的眼睛就看不见它们了。
content.en: The stars are there all day too. Sunlight makes the air so bright that the faint starlight is lost in it, so our eyes cannot pick them out.

title.en: Why Do We Have Four Seasons?

content.zh: 地球是斜着身子绕太阳转的。转到某一边朝向太阳时，白天长、阳光直，就是夏天；转到另一边斜着晒，就是冬天。
content.en: Earth leans over as it goes around the sun. When one side leans towards the sun, days are long and the light is direct — summer. Leaning away gives winter.

title.zh: 月亮为什么会有阴晴圆缺
title.en: Why Does the Moon Change Shape?

content.zh: 月亮自己不发光，靠太阳照亮。它绕着地球转，我们看到被照亮的那半边时多时少，就有了圆缺变化。
content.en: The moon does not shine by itself; the sun lights it. As it circles Earth we see more or less of the lit half, so its shape seems to change.

title.zh: 日食和月食是怎么来的
title.en: What Causes Solar and Lunar Eclipses?

content.zh: 月亮挡在太阳和地球中间，挡住了太阳，这是日食；地球的影子落到月亮上，月亮变暗，这是月食。
content.en: When the moon slips between the sun and Earth it blocks the sun, which is a solar eclipse. When Earth's shadow falls on the moon, that is a lunar eclipse.

title.en: How Big Is the Sun Really?

content.zh: 太阳的直径是地球的 109 倍，里面能装下 130 万个地球。它离我们 1.5 亿公里，所以看着只有一个盘子大。
content.en: The sun is 109 times wider than Earth and could hold 1.3 million Earths. It only looks plate-sized because it sits 150 million km away.

title.zh: 太阳为什么从东边升起
title.en: Why Does the Sun Rise in the East?

content.zh: 地球是自西向东转的，住在地球上的人就看见太阳从东边慢慢升起来，傍晚又从西边落下。
content.en: Earth spins from west to east. Standing on it, we see the sun climb in the east and sink in the west, though it is Earth that is turning.

title.en: Could People Live on the Moon?

content.zh: 月亮上没有空气也没有水，白天 127 度、夜里零下 173 度。人要到那儿住，得自己带上空气和水。
content.en: The moon has no air and no water, with days at 127°C and nights at -173°C. Anyone living there would have to bring air and water along.

title.en: How Were the Constellations Divided?

content.zh: 古人把亮星连成图案，编成故事，再给天空分区。1930 年天文学家统一划成 88 个星座，全世界通用。
content.en: Ancient people joined bright stars into pictures and told stories about them. In 1930 astronomers agreed on 88 constellations covering the whole sky.

title.zh: 冥王星为什么被“开除”了
title.en: Why Was Pluto Dropped as a Planet?

content.zh: 2006 年天文学家给行星定了新标准：要能清干净自己轨道附近。冥王星做不到，就改成了矮行星。
content.en: In 2006 scientists redefined a planet as one that clears its own path. Pluto could not manage that, so it became a dwarf planet.

title.en: What Is Jupiter's Great Red Spot?

content.zh: 那是木星上一场刮了几百年的大风暴，比整个地球还大。风把云卷成旋涡，颜色发红，所以叫大红斑。
content.en: It is a storm on Jupiter that has been blowing for centuries and is bigger than Earth. The winds spin the clouds into a reddish swirl.

title.zh: 光年到底是时间还是距离
title.en: Is a Light-Year Time or Distance?

content.zh: 光年是距离，不是时间。它是光走一年能跑多远，大约 9.5 万亿公里，专门用来量星星之间的远近。
content.en: A light-year is a distance, not a time. It is how far light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion km, used to measure the gaps between stars.

title.en: Why Does the Moon Seem to Follow You?

content.zh: 月亮太远了，你走几百米，看你和月亮的角度几乎没变。近处的树都退到后面，月亮就像一直跟着。
content.en: The moon is so far that walking a few hundred metres barely changes your angle to it. Nearby trees slide past, so the moon seems to tag along.

title.en: How Many Planets Are in the Solar System?

content.zh: 太阳系有八颗行星：水星、金星、地球、火星在内圈，木星、土星、天王星、海王星在外圈。冥王星 2006 年起算矮行星。
content.en: There are eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars inside, then Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Pluto has been a dwarf planet since 2006.

title.zh: 土星为什么能浮在水面上
title.en: Why Would Saturn Float on Water?

content.zh: 土星主要由气体组成，平均密度比水还小。要是有个足够大的浴缸，它真能浮起来，只是它比地球大得多。
content.en: Saturn is mostly gas and is lighter than water overall. Drop it in a big enough bath and it would float, though it is far larger than Earth.

title.zh: 星星为什么有不同的颜色
title.en: Why Are Stars Different Colours?

content.zh: 星星的颜色看表面温度：蓝白色的最热，红色的最凉。我们的太阳是黄色的，温度居中。
content.en: A star's colour shows its surface temperature, with blue-white stars hottest and red ones coolest, and our yellow sun in between.

title.zh: 为什么有的星星特别亮
title.en: Why Are Some Stars Much Brighter?

content.zh: 亮度取决于星星本身有多大、多热，还有离我们多远。又大又近的星星，看着就最亮。
content.en: Brightness depends on the star's size and temperature and on how far away it is, so big, near stars look brightest of all.

title.zh: 北极星为什么总在北边
title.en: Why Does the Pole Star Stay in the North?

content.zh: 北极星几乎正对着地球自转轴的延长线，地球转时它看着不动，所以能用来辨方向。
content.en: The pole star sits almost directly above Earth's axis, so as Earth spins it hardly moves, making it a reliable guide.

title.zh: 北斗七星怎么帮人找方向
title.en: How Does the Big Dipper Show the Way?

content.zh: 把勺口最后两颗星的连线延长约五倍，就找到了北极星，它所在的方向就是正北。
content.en: Extend the line between the two stars at the bowl's edge about five times and you reach the pole star, which marks north.

title.en: How Big Is the Milky Way?

content.zh: 银河系里有一两千亿颗恒星，直径约十万光年。太阳只是其中一条旋臂上的一颗。
content.en: The Milky Way holds one or two hundred billion stars and spans about 100,000 light-years, and our sun is one star on one arm.

title.en: How Big Is the Universe?

content.zh: 我们能看到的宇宙直径约 930 亿光年，之外还有多少没人知道，可能根本看不到边。
content.en: The visible universe is about 93 billion light-years across, and what lies beyond nobody knows, since it may have no edge.

title.en: How Did the Universe Begin?

content.zh: 大多数科学家认为宇宙诞生于约 138 亿年前的一次大爆炸，从那时起一直在膨胀。
content.en: Most scientists think the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago in a Big Bang and has been expanding ever since.

title.zh: 月亮上为什么有那么多坑
title.en: Why Is the Moon Covered in Craters?

content.zh: 月亮没有大气层保护，陨石直接砸下来留下坑。地球有大气，多数陨石在半空就烧掉了。
content.en: With no atmosphere to protect it, meteorites strike the moon and leave craters, while Earth's air burns most of them up first.

title.en: How Was the Moon Formed?

content.zh: 科学家认为，一颗大天体撞上早期的地球，溅出的碎片聚在一起，慢慢变成了月亮。
content.en: Scientists think a large body smashed into the young Earth and the debris thrown out gathered together to form the moon.

title.zh: 太阳为什么会发光发热
title.en: Why Does the Sun Shine?

content.zh: 太阳中心极热极压，氢原子核聚变成氦，同时放出巨大的能量，这就是它的光和热。
content.en: At the sun's core the heat and pressure fuse hydrogen into helium, releasing huge amounts of energy as light and heat.

title.en: How Long Will the Sun Keep Shining?

content.zh: 太阳已经烧了约 46 亿年，还能再烧大约 50 亿年。之后它会膨胀，最后变成一颗白矮星。
content.en: The sun has shone for about 4.6 billion years and has roughly 5 billion left, after which it will swell and end as a white dwarf.

title.en: What Are Sunspots?

content.zh: 黑子是太阳表面磁场很强的地方，那里的温度比周围低一些，所以看着发暗。
content.en: Sunspots are places where the sun's magnetic field is very strong, and being slightly cooler than their surroundings they look dark.

title.en: What Causes the Aurora?

content.zh: 太阳刮来的带电粒子撞进地球大气，把气体分子点亮，就在南北极上空拉出彩色的光幕。
content.en: Charged particles from the sun hit our atmosphere and light up gas molecules, drawing curtains of colour over the poles.

title.en: Where Do Meteorites Come From?

content.zh: 多数陨石来自小行星带的碎片，偶尔也有火星或月亮的石块被撞出来，落到地球上。
content.en: Most come from fragments of the asteroid belt, though now and then a piece of Mars or the moon is knocked loose and lands here.

title.en: Why Do Comets Come Back?

content.zh: 彗星也绕着太阳转，只是轨道又扁又长。哈雷彗星大约每 76 年回到我们眼前一次。
content.en: Comets orbit the sun too but on long, flattened paths, and Halley's comet returns to our skies about every 76 years.

title.en: What Is the Asteroid Belt?

content.zh: 火星和木星之间有一大圈碎石，大的几百公里，小的像石子，它们是没长成行星的废料。
content.en: Between Mars and Jupiter lies a broad ring of rocks, some hundreds of kilometres wide, left over from a planet that never formed.

title.en: Why Is Venus the Hottest Planet?

content.zh: 金星的大气几乎全是二氧化碳，温室效应极强，把热牢牢锁住，表面能到 460 多度。
content.en: Venus has an atmosphere of almost pure carbon dioxide, and a runaway greenhouse effect traps heat, pushing the surface past 460°C.

title.en: How Long Is a Year on Mercury?

content.zh: 水星离太阳最近，跑得也最快，绕太阳一圈只要 88 天，比地球的一年短得多。
content.en: Mercury is closest to the sun and moves fastest, so one trip round takes just 88 days, far shorter than our year.

title.en: Why Does Uranus Spin on Its Side?

content.zh: 天王星的自转轴几乎躺平了，科学家猜测它早年曾被一个大天体撞歪，从此就侧着滚。
content.en: Uranus's axis is tipped almost flat, and scientists think a large body knocked it over long ago, leaving it rolling on its side.

title.zh: 海王星为什么是蓝色的
title.en: Why Is Neptune Blue?

content.zh: 它的大气里有甲烷，甲烷吸收红光、反射蓝光，所以整颗行星看着是深蓝色的。
content.en: Its atmosphere contains methane, which absorbs red light and reflects blue, so the whole planet looks deep blue.

title.en: Is There an Ocean on Europa?

content.zh: 木星的卫星木卫二冰壳下面很可能藏着一片液态水的海洋，水量也许比地球还多。
content.en: Beneath the icy crust of Europa, a moon of Jupiter, lies a likely ocean of liquid water, perhaps holding more water than Earth.

title.en: Is There Life Elsewhere in the Universe?

content.zh: 银河系就有几千亿颗恒星，很多带着行星。还没找到确凿证据，但科学家一直在找。
content.en: The Milky Way alone has hundreds of billions of stars, many with planets, and though there is no proof yet the search goes on.

title.zh: 为什么要把望远镜送上天
title.en: Why Put Telescopes in Space?

content.zh: 大气会晃动星光、挡住不少光线。太空里没有这层干扰，望远镜能看得更远更清楚。
content.en: Our atmosphere blurs starlight and blocks much of it, so in space with no such interference telescopes see further and sharper.

title.zh: 星星为什么会在天上移动
title.en: Why Do Stars Move Across the Sky?

content.zh: 其实是地球在自转，星星看起来才从东往西慢慢移动。夜里拍长时间曝光，能拍出它们的轨迹。
content.en: It is Earth that turns, so stars appear to drift from east to west, and a long night photograph shows their trails as arcs.

title.en: What Happens to a Star When It Grows Old?

content.zh: 小恒星慢慢变成白矮星，大恒星炸成超新星，中心可能塌成中子星甚至黑洞。
content.en: Small stars fade into white dwarfs, while big ones explode as supernovae and their cores may collapse into neutron stars or black holes.

title.en: What Is a Supernova?

content.zh: 大恒星走到尽头时会剧烈爆炸，短时间内亮得能盖过整个星系，爆炸还把新元素撒向宇宙。
content.en: A massive star ends in a violent explosion that briefly outshines a whole galaxy, scattering new elements into space.

title.zh: 星光走了多久才到我们眼里
title.en: How Long Has Starlight Travelled to Reach Us?

content.zh: 太阳光要 8 分多钟，最近的恒星要 4 年多。看到的星光越远，就越是古老的样子。
content.en: Sunlight takes over eight minutes and light from the nearest star over four years, so the further you look the older the light.

title.zh: 太阳系在银河系的什么地方
title.en: Where Is the Solar System in the Milky Way?

content.zh: 我们住在银河系的一条旋臂上，离中心大约两万六千光年，绕银河一圈要两亿多年。
content.en: We sit on one spiral arm about 26,000 light-years from the centre, and one lap of the galaxy takes over 200 million years.

title.zh: 月亮正在离我们远去吗
title.en: Is the Moon Moving Away?

content.zh: 是的，月球每年大约远离地球 3.8 厘米。同时地球自转也在变慢，一天会越来越长。
content.en: Yes, the moon drifts about 3.8 cm further away each year, and Earth's spin slows too, so days slowly get longer.

title.zh: 行星为什么自己不发光
title.en: Why Don't Planets Shine by Themselves?

content.zh: 行星不够大，中心热不到能点燃核聚变的程度。它们只是把太阳的光反射过来。
content.en: Planets are too small for their cores to reach the temperature that starts fusion, so they merely reflect the sun's light.

title.zh: 白天为什么有时能看到月亮
title.en: Why Can You Sometimes See the Moon in Daylight?

content.zh: 月亮在被太阳照亮、又刚好在我们这半边天空时，白天也能看到，只是太阳太亮显得它淡。
content.en: When the moon is lit by the sun and on our side of the sky it shows in daylight, though the bright sun makes it look pale.

title.zh: 为什么月亮和太阳看起来一样大
title.en: Why Do the Moon and Sun Look the Same Size?

content.zh: 太阳比月亮大 400 倍，但也远 400 倍，两个巧合抵消，看起来就差不多大，所以有日全食。
content.en: The sun is 400 times wider than the moon but also 400 times further away, so they look the same size and total eclipses happen.

title.en: How Big Is the Moon?

content.zh: 月亮直径约 3474 公里，只有地球的四分之一多一点。要是地球是个篮球，月亮就是个网球。
content.en: The moon is about 3,474 km across, a little over a quarter of Earth, so if Earth were a basketball the moon would be a tennis ball.

title.en: Does Mars Have Seasons?

content.zh: 有。火星的自转轴也是歪的，一年比地球长，所以每个季节差不多是地球的两倍长。
content.en: Yes, because Mars is tilted like Earth and its year is longer, so each season lasts nearly twice as long as ours.

title.en: Will Saturn's Rings Disappear?

content.zh: 光环是冰块和碎石组成的，正一点点被土星吸走。科学家估计再过几亿年，它们就淡得快看不见了。
content.en: The rings are made of ice and rock and are slowly falling into Saturn, so scientists think they will fade within a few hundred million years.

title.en: Why Is a Comet Like a Dirty Snowball?

content.zh: 彗星的核心是冰混着尘埃和石块。靠近太阳时冰蒸发，拖出长长的彗尾，所以叫它脏雪球。
content.en: A comet's core is ice mixed with dust and rock, and near the sun the ice boils off and streams into a long tail, hence the nickname.
